summary: TLC explored the two-client, one-slide-counter, one-registration model through depth 11 (729 generated / 132 distinct states) with invariants holding; explicit registration restore and both defect toggles were reachable in their bounded checks.

modeled: Two devices merge monotone slide counters in the range 0..2.
A registration delete tombstone at version 1 blocks stale version 0 and allows explicit re-add version 2.
The Worker and Flutter merge paths use deterministic timestamp and tombstone decisions.
abstracted: Question progress payloads, OAuth tokens, and D1 row state are represented by bounded values.
Timestamps are small logical versions 0..2; writes and network operations are abstracted as TLC actions.
out_of_scope: Clock skew, real Cloudflare D1/Worker deployment, OAuth refresh and expiry, device network loss, and production multi-device E2E.
Every possible record, page key, and payload size.
assumptions: A deliberate re-add has an updatedAt greater than the latest known deletedAt.
Worker request ownership comes from a verified session user ID, not the request body.

properties.name: SlideProgressNeverRegresses
properties.meaning: Merging a stale device cannot lower the maximum seen slide count.

properties.name: RegistrationTombstoneWins
properties.meaning: A deleted registration remains absent unless a strictly newer explicit save restores it.
properties.bounds: Clients={c1,c2}; one registration; local/server/delete versions=0..2; depth=11

properties.name: RegistrationRestoreReachable
properties.statement: NoRegistrationRestoreReached is intentionally violated when serverRegistrationAt = 2.
properties.meaning: The model can reach a saved registration whose version is newer than the delete tombstone.

properties.name: SlideMutationDetected
properties.meaning: The slide monotonicity property is sensitive to removing the max merge guard.
properties.bounds: Clients={c1,c2}; slide count=0..2; depth=8; 323 generated / 119 distinct

properties.name: RegistrationMutationDetected
properties.meaning: The tombstone property detects stale-device resurrection when the version guard is removed.
properties.bounds: Clients={c1,c2}; one registration; versions=0..2; depth=7; 228 generated / 89 distinct

findings.title: A deleted exam registration could not be re-added on another sync
findings.property: A newer explicit registration save supersedes its older delete tombstone; stale saves do not.
findings.story: The registration ID is stable for a qualification, round, and phase. The original tombstone was a permanent set entry, so a user could delete a registration and later save the same ID, but the next merge always deleted it again.

reproduction.test: test/user_data_scope_test.dart::re-adding a deleted registration creates a newer sync version; backend/cloudflare/tests/progress.test.js::registration can be re-added only with an update newer than its delete

fix.summary: Store registration tombstones as integer deletion timestamps; choose the save timestamp strictly after the tombstone; merge only records with updatedAt > deletedAt and then clear that tombstone.

sanity_checks: SlideProgressNeverRegresses mutation returns the intended invariant counterexample.
RegistrationTombstoneWins mutation returns the intended invariant counterexample.
NoProgressReached is violated when progress is reachable.
NoRegistrationRestoreReached is violated when explicit restore is reachable.
Normal coverage log contains Learn, MergeProgress, DeleteRegistration, RestoreRegistration, and PushRegistration.

Validate real-device clock behavior, two-device synchronization, session refresh/expiry, and APK/Play release checks.
Keep wrong-note question/answer/explanation/memo content out of progress snapshots.
